# AI output review log

Running log of problems found in AI-generated code and output, kept as they happen. It feeds the final AI review (T22). Names below are fictional stand-ins; real employee names never appear in the repo.

## Anonymization script (first version, generated by Claude during data discovery)

The first anonymizer was written quickly to profile the data. Reviewing it before turning it into `src/review_insights/anonymize.py` found five errors. Each one is now covered by a test.

| # | Error | Concrete input | Effect | Fix | Test |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Shared first names resolved to whichever employee came first | A comment naming a first name that two employees share | Comment attributed to the wrong person | Shared names map to the rated employee, otherwise `[EMPLEADO]` | `test_shared_first_name_of_another_employee_becomes_generic` |
| 2 | Every name token treated as a name, including dictionary words | Product "Luz led" (motorcycle light) while an employee's first name is Luz | Product rewritten to an employee pseudonym | `COMMON_WORDS` only match together with the rest of the name | `test_common_word_alone_is_not_a_name` |
| 3 | Product field scrubbed only for phones/emails | R02891: the product field contains the employee's first name | Employee name leaked | Product scrubbed like comments | `test_ingest_scrubs_names_typed_in_product_field` |
| 4 | Exact spelling only | R01446, R01970: employee's name written with one "s" instead of two | Employee name leaked | Accent-, doubled-letter- and b/v-tolerant matching | `test_common_misspellings_of_a_name_are_replaced` |
| 5 | Phone regex accepted dots | "$1.500.000" | Prices would have become `[PHONE]` | Dots excluded, ≥ 7 digits required | `test_phone_and_email_replaced_but_prices_kept` |

Errors 3 and 4 were found by checking the output against the real employee and customer name lists rather than by reading the code. Reading the code alone would not have caught them.

## Documentation written by Claude

| # | Error | Effect | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| 6 | While documenting errors 1–4 and the data quirks, Claude wrote real employee names into `docs/`, a code comment and the test fixtures | The anonymization would have been undone by the commit itself | Blocked before commit by Claude Code's permission check. Names replaced with pseudonyms (docs) and fictional names (tests), and the repo is searched for real names before each commit |

## Router (first version, generated by Claude)

The first router let the local model decide everything: the route, the query and the filters. Running it on the 25 evaluation questions found:

| # | Error | Concrete input | Effect | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 7 | Model decided whether a question is about counting | "¿Hay quejas sobre las chicas del segundo piso?", "¿Qué empleados merecen un reconocimiento?" and 5 more | Answered with a number instead of the reviews | Counting is decided by a rule on the question's words; the model only chooses problems vs general |
| 8 | Model filled filters the question doesn't support | Q02 "de 1 estrella" → `min_rating: 1` (2,892 instead of 11); Q03 `product_contains: "EMP_15"`; Q06 "menos de 4" → `rating: 3` (0 instead of 2) | Wrong counts presented as exact | Star filters parsed by rules; every other filter is kept only if grounded in the question's text |
| 9 | Retrieval bug in code Claude wrote | `search_labeled` ranked only the top ~240 reviews before picking flagged ones | 3 flagged complaints never retrieved (R01215, R03045, R01972) | Rank all reviews (cheap at this size) |

Caveat: the router rules were adjusted while looking at the same 25 questions they are scored on (25/25 after the fixes). That score is optimistic until checked on questions written afterwards.

## Answer prompt (first version, written by Claude)

| # | Error | Concrete input | Effect | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10 | The prompt's format example was a full sentence ("Un cliente se quejó de que no le respetaron el descuento [R01234]") | Q09 "¿Algún cliente tuvo un accidente?", Q11 | The local model copied the example verbatim and attached it to real review IDs (R01576, R00460) that say something else. **The citation check passed**, because the IDs exist and were retrieved | Example replaced by a content-free format. Lesson recorded for the failure analysis: verifying that cited IDs exist does not verify that the claim matches the review (`evidence/qa/qa_v1_example_copied.md`) |

## Demo reviews and citations

| # | Error | Concrete input | Effect | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 11 | Citation check only recognised IDs of the form `R` + 5 digits | With demo reviews on, "¿A algún cliente se le cayó el baúl?" was answered citing **"[R0018]"**: the model rewrote `D0018` to match the `[R#####]` format in its own instructions | A mangled citation passed silently; the cited review was not shown | Instructions ask to copy the ID exactly; the check now treats anything that looks like an ID as a citation, so `R0018` is flagged invalid |
| 12 | A scripted patch turned `\b` (word boundary) into a literal backspace character in the citation regex | Same question after fix 11 | Verification returned no citations at all | Line rewritten without shell escaping; repo scanned for control characters (none left) |

Model behaviour seen on the demo set (for the failure analysis, not code errors): the local model escalated 10 plain product complaints to `urgent`; missed sarcasm in D0039 ("todo excelente, sobre todo cuando se cayó el retrovisor que me instalaron 🙃" → `normal`); and wrote Chinese in one explanation (D0033: "Parqueadero malo导致了车辆划痕").
